description:
Amaro Ergashev gets the nickname 'the Wet' because of where they work â€” Ironvein's lower infrastructure levels have a chronic condensation problem, and Amaro Ergashev's operation is built into a server room where the ceiling weeps constantly and every surface is furred with gray moisture. They have adapted to this entirely. They wear wicking underlayers always, they've waterproofed every piece of equipment twice, and they have the particular unhealthy pallor of someone who works in artificial light with too much humidity and not enough fresh air. Their Fijian-Zimbabwean heritage gives them a strong frame they've undermaintained into wiry sedentariness, and their hair, naturally coily, is perpetually slightly damp and kept loose around their shoulders. Their eyes are the mod â€” pattern irises in a circuit-board geometry, gold on dark brown, glowing faintly under their own tiny internal bioluminescence. They wear them like a business card.

Amaro Ergashev is the person you go to when you need processing power you shouldn't have â€” stolen cycles from Axiom's distributed architecture, warehoused Tessera storage nodes that fell off a digital truck, bandwidth allocations siphoned from Ferrogate Transit's maintenance grid. They don't ask what the compute is for, they ask how much and when, and they price on urgency. They are not technically gifted in the sense of building new things â€” they are technically gifted in the sense of understanding systems well enough to pick their pockets. They are also deeply, genuinely paranoid, which in their line of work has kept them alive, and socially awkward in the specific way of people who relate more naturally to systems than to people.
